blocks.content: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 gave constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions in India.

rows: Establishment of Gram Sabha at the village level
Representation of MPs and MLAs in local Panchayats
Direct elections to seats at village, intermediate, and district levels
Devolution of powers and 29 functional items under 11th Schedule
Minimum 33% reservation for women across all tiers
Provision of reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs)
5-year fixed term with mandatory re-elections within 6 months of dissolution
Granting financial powers to levy, collect, and appropriate taxes and duties

items: Article 243I mandates the State Finance Commission to be constituted every 5 years by the Governor to review the financial status of Panchayats.
Article 243K vests the superintendence, direction, and control of Panchayat elections in an independent State Election Commission.
Provisions regarding reservations for Backward Classes (OBCs) and devolution of financial powers are voluntary, whereas 33% reservation for women and a 3-tier system are compulsory.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 73rd Amendment Act added Part IX (Articles 243 to 243O) and the 11th Schedule containing 29 functional subjects to the Indian Constitution.
It established a 3-tier Panchayati Raj system at the village, intermediate, and district levels across all states, except those with a population below 20 lakh.
Gram Sabha serves as the primary foundational body comprising all registered voters within a village authority.
Mandates a minimum 33% (one-third) reservation of seats for women, including chairperson positions across all levels.
Fixes a 5-year regular tenure for Panchayats, requiring fresh elections within 6 months in case of early dissolution.
